Also found test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh's Case 30 lockstep array (7 files) is out of this task's file_scope, so adding sapience-publish.sh as an 8th copy of the worktree-checkout-resolution block leaves that global guard incomplete unless file_scope is widened or the gap is explicitly recorded at plan time.

verify-touched.sh's mapped-suite SELECT run for this phase's 4 touched paths (manifest.json edit pulled in 37 broadly-related suites) reported 2 NEW failures: test-mcp-merge-target.sh (Assertion C/E, hand-written MCP entry disturbed) and test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh (case q, a wall-clock timing comparison where NESTED was faster than unguarded). Both build their own isolated fixture manifest.json/mcp-fragment.json unrelated to agent-system/extensions/sapience, reproduced identically on a second standalone run, and are consistent with this machine's current heavy concurrent multi-agent load (dozens of sibling run-all.sh processes observed via ps across other repos) rather than anything this task's edits touch. The OWED fallback set covering the 2 genuinely new files (sapience-publish.sh, test-sapience-publish.sh) ran the full 98-suite battery and passed 98/98. Not fixed as out of file_scope.

sapience-api-lib.sh's sapience_post sets sapience_api_post_http_status via a plain (unexported) global assignment, documented as 'set into the CALLER's shell, since this file is sourced, not subshelled' -- but that guarantee only covers the library FILE being sourced, not the CALL SITE. The idiomatic call pattern every existing consumer uses, response="$(sapience_post ...)", wraps the call in a command substitution, which bash always runs in a subshell regardless of how the function was defined, so sapience_api_post_http_status is silently lost (stays empty in the caller) every time. sapience-project-bind.sh's own tests pass anyway only because its ok-field body check happens to catch the same failure fixtures the status check would have caught. Fixed locally in sapience-publish.sh via a _sapience_post_capture wrapper that redirects sapience_post's stdout to a temp file instead of using $(...), which does not fork a subshell for a plain function call and so preserves the global. Not fixed upstream in sapience-api-lib.sh itself (out of this task's file_scope); a future consumer of sapience_post that needs the HTTP status must use the same redirect-to-tempfile pattern, never $(sapience_post ...).

In sapience-publish.sh's doc-version 409 head_moved handler, 'echo ... | jq ... 2>/dev/null >&2' silently discarded jq's stdout entirely: bash applies redirections left-to-right, so '2>/dev/null' first points fd2 at /dev/null, then '>&2' points fd1 at fd2's CURRENT target (now /dev/null too), discarding both streams instead of the intended 'suppress jq's own stderr, send its stdout to the real stderr'. Fixed by reversing the order to '>&2 2>/dev/null' (dup fd1 to the still-live fd2 first, then redirect fd2 to /dev/null). Caught by test-sapience-publish.sh case 16's own assertion that the server's head object appears in the printed output.

Phase 5's verify-touched.sh re-run over the task's 4 touched paths reproduced the exact same 2 NEW failures already recorded during Phase 1 (test-mcp-merge-target.sh, test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh case(q) -- a wall-clock NESTED-vs-unguarded timing comparison), plus the same 1 pre-existing EXPECTED failure (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh). This confirms the Phase 1 conclusion: these are load-induced/environmental, not caused by this task's edits. All 3 sapience-specific suites (test-sapience-publish.sh, test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh, test-sapience-project-bind.sh) pass cleanly against the deployed tree, and gate 3's provides.scripts parity finding types are absent.
